title: We've Got a Telephone Interview for Morgan Stanley! | The Internship Game #6
description: With two weeks left of the decade, we've finally heard back from Citi, Morgan Stanley, Unilever and Ernst & Young (EY, sorta).  After failing my first year at the university of bristol, I was often told that I would struggle to get by with lower than expected grades, but will this hold through? Let's see just how important failing is in the long run...  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  Twitter:    https://twitter.com/_EbertJ Blog:    https://medium.com/@_EbertJ Instagram:    https://www.instagram.com/ebert_jordan/ eBay:    https://www.ebay.co.uk/usr/ebert_jordan

At long last, we have news of a telephone interview. And this is from Morgan Stanley, of course. I've got some notes up here that I'll go through in a sec. I haven't really finished it out yet. These are just some tech things. Obviously, the questions I expect them to ask me. And these are some general tips of how to succeed how to succeed in a video, in a telephone interview So... yeah, we are going to do that in a sec You can see that I am not very prepared the room's a bit of a mess I've got that chair in the back But... nonetheless telephone, all I need to do is have a voice Yeah, we'll see how that goes in the next it's in 2 hours from now so I'll finish this prep and then hopefully we'll do well hopefully we'll do well Of course about to go phone in hand I always look at the number for this phone instead of this phone because it means i can record obviously why else would i do that but nonetheless i've got my notes up here obviously if you didn't know already you can do this if you put word in read mode it means it's easier to read. Fundamentally that's it! obviously I don't have the questions, these are just the questions I thought would come up and I have natural examples in my head of things that I might be able to use if they do come up uh that's amazing okay thank you very much what unbelievable timing i feel like anyway that that was decent i didn't expect a lot of the questions that came up. The ones that I prepped for obviously weren't. One of them came up, which was the first one, why Morgan Stanley, that's typical. And then they never asked, tell me about yourself. That's what I thought would come up. Usually people ask about things that are in the news or working well on a team. None of those came up, no teamwork leadership. Motivation questions came up. It was purely like... I've got them written down actually, i can't i shouldn't say because that would be super uh probably illegal but i figured while i'm here i might as well talk about the differences again between like video and telephone interview so video interviews are like people prefer video in industry because they can send it to anyone you answer like five separate videos and they can go to 5 different people who can all review it and give you like 5 different scores which they can do anytime anywhere in the world so it's interactive, it's easier for them to like do it and I find it easier to be fair. Obviously you've got to put on a shirt and tie but it's not that big a deal you just talk and then send it off and whatever. it's like, you have to make it seem conversational like oh yeah, you can't literally read off a script because that will make you look very very bad and I mean you shouldn't read if the script anyway it should be very much like a formal interview in real life where you're talking to a person but that that's a bit mad um yeah either way I've done it I think people asked me last time like how would you structure a typical interview answer and it should always be like there's a car method or star method or different ways of doing it car just means context action result and star is situation task action result or something which basically means first you say what it is like if they're asking about how you got in the team you say um a football match you know a public football team that's your context your action is you are losing a half time you went into whatever and did xyz and then the result is that you won or let's say it's a project in uni you can be like your contest was you're doing this project group task of your team the action was you were a bit behind you didn't maybe someone didn't do their work so you had to space out the work to other people and then the result was you got the task done you got a 2-1 uh stuff like that so yeah that's i think that's basically all the questions i had last that i quickly addressed nonetheless um that interview is done we've also heard back from it's quite funny ey messaged me saying um we've changed the methodology of like how we mark our new testing thing and that means that we'd like to re-invite you to an interview and then 20 minutes later they say oh sorry wrong person like i think that's kind of kind of funny damo literally like every week damil bank of america will email me saying like we're still reviewing we're still reviewing we're still reviewing and that's cool i'm happy that they actually update me so i'm not like left in the dark but it can get a bit annoying where i'm like oh maybe i've got it this time and then it just says we're still reviewing but it's fine like i'd rather know than not know um of course morgan stanley just done now i think i mentioned before that i got city rejected i got something else i never actually applied to kpmg i'm gonna do pwc at some point the deadline is in january so there's no rush for that and then i've got a lot of of course engineering um summers that i got applied for and yeah we'll see if I can get something later so another thing is, I forgot to mention that I applied for EdEco CEO for a month . I did it last year but the deadline was like the 27th and I thought that meant the end of day 27th what that meant was end of day 26th so when I logged in on the 27th or whatever day it was they said you're late, you can't do it so that was super annoying so this year i got in really early and just did it um right off the bat i think the deadline is in february but i've already got it submitted of course as i said pwc i'll do at some point um and yeah i'm also back to greensill they seem like a very exciting firm green saw like supply chain financing so i've done some of that and then again these are all like spring positions when it comes to engineering stuff that's all gonna be summer, hopefully I can get summer out the way. Sadly, I wasn't allowed to do a year of industry or placement, which would've been a lot easier I feel like and a little less stressful. But nonetheless we move, we move and hopefully the next time I do this we'll have something in the bank be it, an assessment center that would be super cool or Unlikely but also possible, it would be an actual internship or Spring Week and yeah, let's see So finally end of day obviously today I did the called earlier Morgan Stanley call and all that stuff I can do for you That's what you do So, finally Ha! End of day Obviously today I did the call earlier Morgan Stanley Call Its now just past midnight On Thursday 12th of December And Its been an interesting flow I mean, if you haven't already realised Im doing these videos every Friday Which means Every other Friday Sorry I'm uploading on Fridays now And obviously you can do other series going on as well The flip challenge Which will update you on very very soon but i mean let me briefly show you this spreadsheet so as you can see i've deleted a few things uni lever as you just saw got rejected from uh green silver i applied to recently and yeah i'm waiting back for those four in the middle that i've done interviews for and then the other ceo for a month and two at the bottom are things that i've applied for. i'm still waiting for to see if i progress do i do an interview or whatever.
